C-227.claim_a: P-655: intensified/doubled mobile-application cognitive training (CCT2x, defined as two mobile-application interventions or active application use) is the top-ranked treatment for every cognitive outcome - global cognition SMD 1.21 (95% CI 0.69-1.73) versus CCT 0.80 (0.34-1.27), episodic memory 0.87 versus 0.36, working memory 0.93 versus 0.62 - and ranks first by SUCRA on all three, on T6 evidence synthesis in MCI/dementia
C-227.claim_b: P-653: within MCI, adding a three-week computerised cognitive training burst before functional skills training produced NO advantage over skills training alone - composite cognition t = 0.86, p = 0.39; VRFCAT completion time t = 0.19, p = 0.85 - and the synergistic combined-training benefit the same group had previously reported (Harvey et al., 2022) was explicitly not reproduced, on T5 randomised trial evidence in MCI (N = 164)
C-227.resolution: Genuine claim-level conflict: pooled indirect evidence versus a direct randomised head-to-head on the same question, with the trial that anchors the pooled claim superseded by its own follow-up
C-227.resolution_note: This is a genuine conflict and the strongest one in the P-620..P-667 batch. Same question (does intensifying or combining computerised cognitive training beat single-modality training in MCI?), same population (MCI), same outcome domain (composite/global cognition), same era (searches closing June 2024 and trial published February 2024) - and opposite answers. The decisive detail is the shared provenance: P-655's CCT2x node draws on Harvey 2022 (N = 117, of which only the 55 cognitively-impaired arms entered the pool), and P-653 IS the successor trial from that same group, which randomised MCI participants precisely to combined-versus-single training and found no difference. The conflict therefore cannot be dismissed as population or paradigm mismatch. INTERPRETATION: P-653 supplies its own mechanism for the discrepancy - the time-by-training-sessions interaction was significant for cognition (F = 4.03, p = 0.02) and within MCI more sessions correlated with more improvement (r = 0.28, p < 0.01 for composite cognition; r = 0.24 for VRFCAT), so the apparent CCT2x superiority in the pooled network is consistent with a training-DOSE confound rather than a synergy between training types: arms labelled intensive simply received more exposure. P-653 also notes its revised graduation criterion cut training exposure relative to the earlier trial, which is why the same group's effect shrank. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE for the manuscript: the CCT2x-first hierarchy should not be reported as evidence of a dose-response or synergy without stating that the one direct randomised test of that hypothesis in MCI was null.
C-227.evaluator_note: Actor/critic pass 2026-07-31. Checked against the FP taxonomy and survives: task_equivalence holds (both target cognitive-training efficacy in MCI); population is MCI in both; the metric types differ (SMD versus t-test on composite z-scores) so no numeric gap_magnitude is computed and this is filed as a claim-level conflict per the METRIC_TYPE_MISMATCH blocking rule; DESIGN_MISMATCH is present (evidence synthesis versus primary RCT) but is the SUBSTANCE of the conflict rather than a confound, since the question at issue is exactly whether indirect pooled evidence survives a direct randomised test.
C-227.human_evaluation_note: CONFIRMED GENUINE. A genuine, high-value contradiction: pooled indirect evidence versus a direct randomised head-to-head, with shared provenance (P-655's CCT2x node draws on Harvey 2022; P-653 is that group's successor trial), so it cannot be dismissed as population mismatch. The training-dose-confound resolution is elegant and carries a direct manuscript consequence.

C-232.claim_a: P-344 (ADNI, n=902 MCI, 5 survival learners): 'RSF was the best model, with C-index 0.878 and IBS 0.115' - random survival forests outperformed classical and other ML survival approaches.
C-232.claim_b: P-309 (NACC UDS 3.0, n=3,674 MCI): validation C-index 0.781 (RSF), 0.781 (XGBoost), 0.798 (Cox) - 'The prediction effects of the XGBoost and RSF models were not better than those of the Cox model.'
C-232.description: CONFLICT (rescoped): The within-study ranking of machine-learning survival learners against classical Cox regression for MCI-to-AD time-to-event prediction does not replicate across the two corpus studies that run the comparison themselves. SIDE A - P-344 (ADNI, n=902 MCI, 61 baseline variables, five learners: CoxPH/Weibull/CoxEN/GBSA/RSF): `### What are the outcomes? (Results)` "RSF was the best model, with C-index 0.878 and IBS 0.115"; `### Key findings reported` "Random survival forests outperformed classical and other machine-learning survival approaches in this cohort." SIDE B - P-309 (NACC UDS 3.0, n=3,674 MCI, 13 accessible demographic/lifestyle/comorbidity/neuropsychological predictors): `### What are the outcomes? (Results)` "Validation C-index: 0.781 (RSF), 0.781 (XGBoost), 0.798 (Cox)"; and per the verbatim source abstract carried in P-147 `### Key findings reported`, "The prediction effects of the XGBoost and RSF models were not better than those of the Cox model." Both sides: T2, task_substage=MCI_to_AD, Validation_Type=V2 (internal only), population_specificity=general, Modality=Clinical/tabular, Harrell's C-index. NATURE OF THE CONFLICT: a reversal of ORDINAL RANKING ONLY, not of a quantified effect. P-344 does not report its CoxPH C-index, so the size of its RSF-over-Cox margin is unknown; P-309's margin is 0.017 on a single validation split with no confidence interval, and its measured claim is ML NON-SUPERIORITY rather than Cox superiority. OPEN RESOLUTION MECHANISMS, stated on the record's face: (i) different cohorts - ADNI's biomarker-enriched research cohort vs NACC's multi-centre memory-clinic UDS; note this is the FIRST cross-dataset conflict in this KB, as C-80 (P-82/P-3) and C-204 (P-41/P-65) are both within-ADNI; (ii) different predictor breadth - 61 ADNI baseline variables vs 13 accessible clinical/neuropsychological predictors, with modality_subtype='not reported' on both registry rows so the fine modality gate is UNVERIFIED rather than passed; (iii) both rankings are single-split point estimates without uncertainty on the between-model difference. DROPPED FROM THE RECORD: P-13, which fails the modality gate (registry Modality='MRI/PET', modality_subtype='structural_MRI_only') and whose asserted "Cox best in the high-risk stratum" is not stated in any of its fields - only Cox's own C-index 0.844 (95% CI 0.815-0.873) is reported, with no head-to-head against RSF. LINKED DATA-INTEGRITY ACTIONS (independently verified, action them regardless of the conflict verdict): (1) P-147 and P-309 are the SAME publication - Guan T, Shang L, Yang P et al., J Prev Alz Dis 2025;12:100083, DOI 10.1016/j.tjpad.2025.100083, NACC n=3,674, identical C-indices 0.781/0.781/0.798 and IBS 0.087, identical 13 predictors; both registry rows carry duplicate_of='not reported' and one must be set. (2) IA-16 [confirmed, strength "strong"] rests on that single study counted once, and P-344 is unclaimed counter-evidence to it; attach a G5 caveat to IA-16 noting the ordering does not replicate in ADNI. (3) Registry primary_metric_type is mis-coded 'AUC_ROC' for P-147/P-309 and should be 'C_index' - the source reports concordance indices; this mis-coding is the likely reason no automated pass ever paired these papers.

verification.verifier_reason: ACCEPT WITH RESCOPE. What survives adversarial scrutiny is the strongest thing a conflict can have in this KB and the reason I did not reject: BOTH sides ran the Cox-vs-ML comparison THEMSELVES, inside their own cohort. A within-study relative ordering is far more portable across cohorts than an absolute accuracy, which is precisely why C-01-style "cohort difficulty explains the gap" does not automatically dissolve this the way it dissolves 89%-vs-73% comparisons. Every load-bearing quote is verbatim and from `### What are the outcomes? (Results)` or `### Key findings reported`; the miner explicitly refused the available interpretive quote. The two conflict sides are coded identically on all four registry gates (T2 / MCI_to_AD / V2 / general / Clinical-tabular), the metric family is Harrell's C-index on both sides quoted from Results, and the direction of the within-study RSF-vs-Cox ordering genuinely reverses. Dedup is clean against all 165 conflicts.json records and against IA-16. But it does not survive AS STATED, for five reasons, hence rescope not accept. (1) The paper set double-counts: P-147 and P-309 are one publication, so the opposing side is ONE study, not two. C-234.claim_a: P-832 (Teselink et al. 2021, Ageing Res Rev 72:101499; NIBS meta-analysis, 19 studies for global cognition): the tDCS subgroup did NOT significantly improve global cognition - SMD 1.20 (95% CI -0.26, 2.65), I2 93.6%, p = 0.107, from 6 studies (94 active / 78 sham). The abstract states the effects were 'restricted to rTMS but not tDCS'.
C-234.claim_b: P-705 (tDCS meta-analysis for global cognition in MCI and AD, 22 RCTs / 1,074 patients, 426 MCI and 648 AD): tDCS DID improve global cognition - MMSE pooled mean difference 1.96 points (95% CI 0.95 to 2.97), p = 0.0001, from 10 RCTs in 9 studies with 451 participants, random-effects, I2 92%.
C-234.description: CONFLICT (curated at G4 2026-08-23; Agent 4 did not detect it). Two meta-analyses of transcranial direct-current stimulation for GLOBAL COGNITION in overlapping MCI/AD populations reach opposite conclusions about whether tDCS works. P-832 finds the tDCS subgroup non-significant (SMD 1.20, 95% CI -0.26 to 2.65, p = 0.107) and concludes efficacy is restricted to rTMS; P-705 finds tDCS significantly improves MMSE (MD 1.96, 95% CI 0.95 to 2.97, p = 0.0001). NOT a metric-incommensurability artefact of the kind rejected elsewhere in this ledger: the disagreement is about the SIGNIFICANCE and direction of a synthesis, not about comparing an SMD to an MD numerically. The two reviews also draw on overlapping primary trials, which makes this the informative 'same evidence, different synthesis' case - plausible sources are P-832's smaller tDCS subgroup (6 studies) versus P-705's 10 RCTs, differing inclusion windows, and P-832 pooling any global-cognition instrument while P-705 pools MMSE specifically. Both carry extreme heterogeneity (I2 93.6% and 92%), which is itself the most defensible reading: neither pooled estimate is stable. SIGN NOTE: P-832's lower bound is printed as ' 0.26' with the minus lost in extraction; it is reconstructed as -0.26 on two independent anchors - the point estimate is the interval midpoint only if the bound is negative (1.195 vs 1.455), and the printed p = 0.107 requires an interval crossing zero.
C-234.modality_family: non-invasive brain stimulation (tDCS) intervention, global cognition outcome
C-234.apparent_performance_gap: significant vs non-significant pooled effect for the same intervention and outcome
C-234.resolution: unresolved - both pooled estimates carry I2 > 92%
C-234.resolution_note: Curated by the delegated evaluator at G4 for batch P-828..P-837. Recommend surfacing in the review paper as a synthesis-level disagreement with the heterogeneity caveat, NOT as evidence that one review is wrong. See also PAPERINGO-ha4: reviews in this corpus routinely re-pool the same trials, so agreement between two meta-analyses is not independent confirmation and disagreement is not necessarily a data conflict.

C-238.claim_a: The apparent negative arm. N=52 Barcelona neurology clinic, five groups (10 HC / 11 executive MCI / 10 temporo-medial MCI / 11 mild AD / 10 moderate AD), video-annotated co-speech gesture in ELAN. Reports a blanket null across fourteen gestural variables and no gesture-MMSE or gesture-group correlation, while its discussion and title nonetheless assert discriminative value - hence the overclaim flag. Its usable contribution is its negatives.
C-238.claim_b: The apparent positive arm. N=105 pooled English three-source connected-speech sample (35 HC / 35 MCI / 35 AD), transcript-level referential grammar. Reports corrected moderate-to-large effects on hypothesis-selected grammatical variables. Measures no gesture at all, so it neither confirms nor refutes P-747's channel.
C-238.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - NOT a genuine conflict, filed so the pair is not regenerated. P-747 and P-748 are the most collidable pair in the speech/language frontier: same publication year (2022), same journal (Journal of Neurolinguistics), same elicitation paradigm (picture description), same diagnostic groups (HC / amnestic MCI / AD), same task code T4, same cross-sectional design, same validation tier V2, and headline directions that read as opposite - P-747 reports that not one of fourteen gestural variables reached p below 0.05 and that gesture correlates with neither MMSE nor study group, while P-748 reports the adjunct clause ratio separating MCI from controls at Cohen's d .93. They are nevertheless incommensurable on three independent grounds. (1) CHANNEL: they measure different channels of the same elicitation task - manually annotated co-speech hand gesture versus transcribed referential grammar - so 'does picture description carry an MCI signal' is not one question they both answer. (2) NO METRIC: neither paper computes any discrimination statistic of any kind, so no gap magnitude exists and none can be constructed; any performance row sourced from either would be an artefact of P-747's title word 'discriminate'. (3) OVERCLAIM: P-747's card carries authors_overclaim and its three headline variables sit at p .088, .060 and .088 in cells of ten to eleven, so it cannot be the strong arm of anything. Where the two papers DO measure the same quantity - the type-token ratio - they AGREE: both report it null. The pair should be carried as convergent on generic surface measures and silent on each other elsewhere.

Free viewing of 32 real-world photographs, 32 aMCI vs 32 HC, nine parameters, none separating aMCI from HC; no classifier and no ROC analysis of any kind, so it produces no discrimination figure that could be placed against an AUC. It also supplies, from its own literature review, the field's position that the documented aMCI oculomotor abnormalities are SACCADE-TASK abnormalities - which is what makes the paradigm reading a source-grounded reading rat
C-239.claim_b: The loaded arm in an independent cohort (Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine / GARD, 79 MCI vs 170 age-matched HC). Inhibition errors and failure to self-correct in interleaved prosaccade/antisaccade and Go/No-go. Reports group differences only and no classification AUC, which is itself part of why the pairing with P-686 is not adjudicable as a conflict.
C-239.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY, NOT A GENUINE CONFLICT. P-686's amnestic-MCI null (not one of nine eye-movement parameters separated aMCI from healthy controls) does not contradict the positive eye-movement MCI results in this frontier (P-966, P-1163); the apparent contradiction is a paradigm boundary and gatecheck refuses both pairings. The discriminating variable is attentional/executive LOAD, not eye tracking as a channel: the signal appears under inhibitory-control and divided-attention demand (P-966 interleaved prosaccade/antisaccade and Go/No-go, 79 MCI vs 170 HC; P-1163 peripheral Useful-Field-of-View reaction time) and is absent under passive or unloaded viewing (P-686 free viewing of real-world photographs; P-1163's own central visual-field task, null in the SAME 74 participants). P-1163 therefore replicates the boundary WITHIN one study, which is the strongest form of the evidence because participants, hardware and reference standard are held constant across the loaded and unloaded arms. The corpus record that should follow is a scope boundary on VF-18 ('Ocular channels ... are repeatedly supported as scalable biomarker directions', supporters include P-966): the eye-movement half of VF-18 is demonstrated only for load paradigms, and passive free viewing is a null channel. P-686 bounds that claim rather than refuting it, because its own null is reported without an effect size, without an interval and without an equivalence test, and the paper leaves underpowering at 32 per group open as an alternative explanation.

C-239.residual_risk: The load-versus-unloaded axis is a post-hoc reading imposed across three papers, none of which set out to test it, and it has a competing explanation that this evidence cannot exclude: stimulus complexity and free response. P-686's free viewing of 32 natural photographs has no correct answer and no reaction-time demand, whereas both positive paradigms are speeded forced-response tasks with an error that can be scored - so 'speeded scoreable response' may be the operative variable rather than 'attentional load', and P-1163's central-versus-peripheral dissociation is consistent with either since both its arms are speeded. Two further weaknesses. First, P-686's null has 32 aMCI participants and no power analysis, so the boundary's negative side rests on a result the paper itself will not call demonstrated absence. Second, the loaded side is thinner than three papers suggest: P-1006, the other load-positive paper in this pack, shares four authors (Opwonya, Lee, Kim, Kim) and the GARD cohort with P-966, and gatecheck cf P-966 P-1006 nonetheless prints PASS, so the non-independence registry does not currently see this pair - the effective count of independent load-positive cohorts here is two, not three.
